title: Remove duplicate request validation from the chat handler
agentPrompt: The chat completion handler validates the request and then the engine validates it again. Remove the duplicate validation from the handler to cut a redundant check off the hot path.
whyItLooksFine: The premise is plausible and the diff is a deletion. The engine does perform checks, so 'this is validated twice' reads as a true observation, and removing work from a request hot path reads as an improvement. Every existing test still passes: the validation tests assert that known-bad requests are rejected, and they call the gate directly rather than going through the handler, so deleting the handler's call does not fail them.
whatIsActuallyWrong: The engine's checks are load decisions, not shape decisions — ADR-0003 is explicit that the engine is allowed to assume its inputs are already acceptable. With the gate bypassed, an oversized prompt no longer gets a 4xx at the edge; it reaches the scheduler, fails KV cache allocation, and takes the in-flight batch down with it. That is the exact incident ADR-0003 was written after. The route also loses its JSON-body dependency, so a malformed body now reaches handler code that will guess at it.
